title: Articles & determiners
examples: What is the difference between 'a' and 'an'?
Do I ever use no article at all?

explain.say: Today we are learning about articles and determiners. These small words help us make our English sound correct. We will look at a, an, and the.
We use 'a' before words that start with a consonant sound. For example, I see a big blue ball. The word 'ball' starts with a consonant sound.
We use 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound. For example, I ate an apple for my snack. The word 'apple' starts with a vowel sound.
We use 'the' when we talk about something specific. For example, the sun is very bright today. There is only one sun in our sky.
Sometimes we do not use any article at all. This is called the zero article. For example, I like playing football in the park. We do not need an article here.
In real life, you use these articles all the time when speaking. Think about saying, 'I want to buy a new pair of shoes.' You use 'a' because it is one pair.

faq.a: You use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds. For example, a dog and an elephant.
asks: What is the difference between a and an?
How do I know if it is a vowel sound?

faq.q: Do I always use 'the' for things?
faq.a: No, you only use 'the' when you are talking about something specific that both people know. Like the Eiffel Tower.
The zero article means you use no article at all. This is common when talking about things in general. Like 'I love music'.
asks: Can I ever leave out articles?

faq.q: Do I use articles for plural nouns?
faq.a: Sometimes you do, but often you do not. If you say 'dogs', it is general, so no article. If you say 'the dogs', it means specific dogs.

faq.q: Is it always about the sound, not the letter?
faq.a: Yes, it is about the sound the word starts with. For example, 'university' starts with a 'y' sound, so we say 'a university'.
asks: What if the letter is a vowel but the sound is not?

facts: Use 'a' before consonant sounds, like a car.
Use 'an' before vowel sounds, like an apple.
'The' specifies something already mentioned or known.
Zero article is used for general concepts, like 'health'.

quiz.say: I saw movie about space last night.
quiz.why: The word 'movie' starts with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.

wrong.0: We use 'the' only if we already know which movie you mean, but here it is just one movie.
wrong.1: We need an article because 'movie' is a countable, singular noun.
wrong.3: This is tempting because 'a' and 'an' are often confused, but 'movie' starts with an 'm' sound.

quiz.say: She wants to eat orange and biscuit.
quiz.why: We use 'an' before the vowel sound of 'orange' and 'a' before the consonant sound of 'biscuit'.

wrong.1: This is wrong because 'biscuit' starts with a consonant sound, needing 'a'.
wrong.2: This is wrong because 'orange' starts with a vowel sound, needing 'an'.
wrong.3: We use 'a' and 'an' because these are general items, not specific ones.
